item.title: Dhaka tops AQI rankings with ‘very unhealthy’ air quality
item.description: Dhaka recorded the worst air quality in the world on Sunday morning, topping the global pollution index as residents continued to breathe air classified as very unhealthy.According to data from air quality monitoring organisation IQAir, Bangladesh's capital ranked first on the global air pollution list as of 10:20 AM on Sunday, with an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 299.India’s Kolkata followed in second place with a score of 218, also placing it in the “very unhealthy” category.An AQI score b

item.title: Cold wave eases in northern Bangladesh as temperature rises
item.description: After weeks of biting cold, signs of early spring are emerging in Bangladesh’s northernmost districts, with temperatures rising and daily life returning to normal.The severe cold wave that gripped Panchagarh has eased by mid-Magh, bringing relief to residents and workers alike.According to local weather data, the temperature in Panchagarh rose to 11 degrees Celsius at 9:00 AM on Sunday.The end of the prolonged cold spell has resulted in clear, fog-free mornings and bright sunshine across the dis

item.title: 2 friends killed as truck hits bike in Dhaka
item.description: Two friends were killed after a truck hit their motorcycle in Dhaka's Jatrabari area early Sunday.The deceased were identified as Khayrul Hossain Kamrul, 20, and Yasin Rana 27.It was learnt that, the two friends met the accident at an early hours while returning from a wedding programme of one of their friends. item.title: Shakib Al Hasan cleared for selection as BCB signals possible return
item.description: Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) has confirmed that former captain Shakib Al Hasan is once again eligible for national team selection, marking a major development amid Bangladesh’s recent exclusion from the T20 World Cup.The decision followed a lengthy eight-hour BCB board meeting that concluded late on Saturday night. item.title: 20,000km of canals to be excavated across country: Tarique Rahman
item.description: BNP Chairman Tarique Rahman has said that if the party comes to power, it will excavate 20,000 kilometers of canals across the country.
